questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The crucial aspect for me was that they had interesting and relevant courses and that it was a place where people spoke english, as I didn't want to be segregated from 'normal students' in courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very good experience and I learned alot, and I've come home with alot of new perspectives on the practices in my own university.

questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was very much like my home university (Cph)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very much the same style. There is more emphasis on critical thinking in Manchester than in Copenhagen. We also had sightly more lectures in small classes with only 15 people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Racisms and ethnicity in the UK
Black identities and cultures in Latin America
Social Thought from the global south

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Social Thought from the global south - it was really interesting. I was taught about thinkers you'de never heard of before in Copenhagen mainly because they're from the global south and the social sciences at Copenhagen Uni aren't that critical towards their own positioning in the world.

questions.answer: Manchester is a really fun city with alot of concerts and shows, so I spend a bit more on that than I expected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was just a bit cheaper than i Denmark. Except vegetables.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is an endless amout of clubs and social activities at Manchester uni. I was personally in the Hiking Society and in the Arts and Craft Society

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hiking. There is so much beautiful nature really close by manchester. Go to concerts and shows as well as it is a quite iconic city music-wise. All museums are also free and there are plenty of good ones in Manchester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy - people in Manchester are really welcoming and helpful

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The university basically does it for you with all the clubs and societies

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The traffic

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openess

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. there is normally no utensils in the student kitchens and everybody just buy there own, so try to see if you can come in contact with an exchange student that is already in Manchester to take over their stuff when they leave. 
2. Come a bit earlier than when your semester starts to have time to travel a bit in the contry
3. remember your umbrella

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Its a very pleasant place to go on exchange, its all very easy and there is alot to do

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The courses and the friends that I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The traffic and the rain

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
